clinician.final_diagnosis: Definite Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndrome (PNS) associated with Papillary Thyroid Cancer (PTC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old male smoker presented with a 2-year history of progressive gait disorder and poor balance. Neurological examination revealed horizontal nystagmus, intention tremor, and ataxic gait. Cerebral MRI demonstrated significant bilateral cerebellar atrophy in the superior vermis. Initial laboratory workup showed normal hemogram, biochemical tests, and thyroid function tests, but elevated anti-thyroid peroxidase and anti-thyroglobulin antibodies. Malignancy screening (including thyroid ultrasonography and PET/CT) revealed an 11×9 mm hypoechoic nodule in the left thyroid lobe with elevated FDG uptake (SUV max 7.22). Bilateral total thyroidectomy was performed, and pathological examination confirmed papillary thyroid cancer (PTC). Onconeural antibodies (anti-Hu, anti-Yo, anti-Ri, anti-amphiphysin, anti-Tr, anti-PPCA-2, anti-Ma, anti-CV-1, anti-ANNA-3) were negative. The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (0.4 g/kg for 10 days), which resulted in partial improvement of ataxia (SARA score 20/40). Radioactive iodine treatment was subsequently initiated, and thyroid replacement therapy was started for permanent hypothyroidism. At 6-month follow-up, the SARA score remained 20/40. The diagnosis of 'definite' PNS was established based on the presence of a classical cerebellar syndrome with cancer (PTC) developing within 5 years of neurological symptom onset, without requirement for onconeural antibodies.
